vikram_sre: heads up — seeing very skewed routing for `svc/gpu-serving` in us-west-2. One node (10.0.3.42) is getting ~70% of new connections, others <10%. Client retries/5xx have jumped (~15% 502/504s). Started ~02:00 UTC after the cluster kernel rollout. ipvs stats show stuck sessions to that dest. Anyone seen this before?

infra-bot: [ALERT] svc/gpu-serving high connection concentration on node 10.0.3.42 (detected 2026-02-15T02:12:14Z)

ana_infra: can you paste `ipvsadm -Ln --stats` and `kubectl get ep -n inference gpu-serving -o wide` and maybe `kubectl get pods -o wide` for the backend pods? Also any kernel version diffs on the nodes that are hot vs cold.

vikram_sre: posting trimmed outputs — hot node is the one that got the new kernel.
```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.96.0.42:443 rr
  -> 10.0.3.42:443                Masq    1      3245       0
  -> 10.0.3.43:443                Masq    1       40       0
  -> 10.0.3.44:443                Masq    1       33       0
  -> 10.0.4.10:443                Masq    1       12       0
```

# kubectl get ep -n inference gpu-serving -o wide
NAME         ENDPOINTS                       AGE
gpu-serving  10.0.3.42:443,10.0.3.43:443...  3d
```

vikram_sre: conn counts are real — we instrumented per-pod TCP accepts: pod on 10.0.3.42 showing ~3k active accepts, others tiny.

matt_engineering: interestingly, I saw packet-loss counters and RX errors spike on the hot node 10.0.3.42 right after the kernel bump (5.12 -> 5.13). Also MTU was changed to 9000 on that rack last week for RoCE testing. Could be GRO/LRO/GSO regression causing asymmetric behavior or fragmentation.

chandra_net: RDMA/RoCE presence makes this far more plausible — if jumbo frames are misconfigured on some hops, path MTU discovery can fail and TCP can degrade. IPVS selection should still be round-robin, but if syn/syn-ack RTTs or retrans patterns favor a particular backend (or conn reuse keeps hitting the same dest) you can see stickiness. Also check neighbor/ARP flapping and NIC offloads.

ana_infra: quick checks:
- `ethtool -k` on the hot vs cold nodes (GRO/GSO settings)
- `ip -s link` to see packet drops/mismatched MTU
- `conntrack -L | grep <svc-port>` to see conntrack explosion
- `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward` and `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`

vikram_sre: ran those: hot node had GRO=on, others GRO=off (weird). `ip -s link` showed RX dropped 4k packets on that interface. conntrack table had many ESTABLISHED entries pinned to that backend.

oncall_rosemary: mitigation steps we tried: 1) drained the hot node -> traffic redistributed immediately; 2) toggled GRO off on the hot NIC -> traffic normalized; 3) temporarily rolled back the kernel on that node -> stable. So seems tied to kernel + NIC offload interaction.

matt_engineering: that matches known regressions where GSO/GRO handling changed in 5.13 with certain Intel drivers. If GRO causes the node to coalesce packets and upstream components drop fragments, TCP behavior can favor some connections. File a kernel/driver bug but for immediate safety we should: pin affected nodes to the older kernel, disable GRO on all nodes in the rack, and add an autoscale rollback runbook.

chandra_net: long term: ensure MTU and offload settings are enforced via CNI/node bootstrap (daemonset that enforces ethtool/mTU), and add a net-health probe that alerts on per-node RX drops and GRO/GSO mismatch. Also add an ipvs health check that compares ActiveConn across endpoints and alerts on >x:1 skew.

ana_infra: alternative quick mitigation we discussed: switch kube-proxy to iptables mode on the cluster while we triage ipvs kernel issue. iptables will be heavier CPU-wise but often sidesteps ipvs kernel path bugs. Thoughts?

vikram_sre: we did a canary switch on the dev cluster (ipvs -> iptables) and saw more even spread but higher CPU on nodes. For prod we prefer the pin/disable-offload route for now.

oncall_rosemary: created follow-up tickets:
- INFRA-8492: pin kernels for the affected hosts and add rollback playbook (priority P0)
- NET-7211: daemonset to enforce MTU/offload and net probes (P1)
- SRE-4533: add ipvs skew alert and docs for iptables fallback (P2)

vikram_sre: summary: root cause likely NIC driver/GRO regression interacting with jumbo MTU (RoCE test) after kernel upgrade -> packet drops and conn skew to one backend. Immediate fixes: drain + pin kernel + disable GRO on rack. Long term: enforce config via daemonset, net probes, and open bug with distro/driver.

ana_infra: thanks — I'll run the pin/daemonset changes in the morning and coordinate with platform for a quieter kernel rollout window. :thumbsup:

matt_engineering: filing kernel bug with vendor now (link will go in NET-7211).

chandra_net: +1, will draft the ipvs skew alert query.

vikram_sre: closing the loop here — traffic looks stable after drain + GRO toggle. Reopen if we see reoccurences. :white_check_mark:
